extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants (individuals and organizations) submitting an Online Funding Inquiry (OFI) to the John Templeton Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing the John Templeton Foundation Online Funding Inquiry form: how to describe the project, required fields, personnel and organizational information, budget rules, and capital expenditure and review constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project term / duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A project has a specific start and end date; generally projects submitted may have a term of no more than 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum permissible duration depends on the type of organization: for most organizations recognized as U.S. public charities, Proposed Project End Date must be no more than 36 months beyond Proposed Project Start Date; for all other organizations and grants to individuals, the Proposed Project End Date should not be more than 33 months beyond the Proposed Project Start Date. For grants requiring Expenditure Responsibility (ER), JTF has its own internal project duration maximum of 33 months which may limit funding for capital expenditures with useful life >3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cycle and funding area selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the funding cycle and the Funding Area that best align with your proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation accepts OFIs any time but reviews them at specific times depending on request size—consult the grantmaking calendar to select the appropriate cycle. If unsure of the best Funding Area, select the closest fit; the OFI will be triaged and routed internally to the appropriate department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Title clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Title should clearly, concisely, and in non-technical terms convey the essence of your proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep title short and understandable to non-specialists; avoid technical jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Summary content and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe what you plan to do, why it is worth doing, and what impact the project will have; written for a general intellectually engaged reader (e.g., New York Times or London Times reader), not necessarily a specialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good Executive Summary will briefly answer: (a) What specific questions will the project help to answer? (b) What activities will you carry out to answer those questions? (c) Why is this project needed? (d) What concrete deliverables will you produce by the end of the project? (e) What impact will your project have? Do not include information about the project team, organization, request amount, or project duration in the Executive Summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description detail and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a specific, concise, and detailed description of the activities you plan to carry out with the requested funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the longest and most important field in the OFI. If special characters, graphs, figures, or formatting are required, upload a document in the provided space and type 'See attached document' in the form to refer staff to the upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the current conditions in the relevant field(s), identify the problems the project will address, and articulate the specific opportunity the project presents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the issue matters and how the project fits into the existing landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (deliverables)
rubrics_metrics.description: List the important events and work products (outputs) that your project activities will generate and that are necessary to make progress toward Outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear list of outputs you intend to produce; these are sometimes called deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (goals, results, impacts) and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the specific and identifiable changes you expect your outputs will bring about (or contribute to) within 5 years of your project's end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes should describe what success looks like for the project; be specific and identify the timeframe (within 5 years of project end).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for Success
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why your team and/or organization is positioned to be successful in this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe relevant experience, institutional support, infrastructure, and capabilities that make the project likely to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Donor Intent / Templeton vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the proposed project would advance the philanthropic vision of Sir John Templeton and align with his Donor Intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Foundation's Funding Areas page for more information on donor intent and funding priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to prior Templeton grants
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the proposed work is similar to or expands work from an active or closed grant you or your organization received from JTF, Templeton World Charity Foundation, or the Templeton Religion Trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, explain (a) how the proposed project is similar to, builds upon, furthers, or expands the prior work, and (b) provide Project Title, Grant ID#, Grant Amount, end date, and a very brief synopsis of the prior project's activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Project Start Date timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Proposed Project Start Date should consider the Foundation's review timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Proposed Project Start Date should be at least 6 weeks after the end of the relevant funding cycle (i.e., the applicant notification date). Consult the grantmaking calendar before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Contact and communication responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Primary Contact is the person who will manage all communications with the Foundation regarding the funding request; the originator of the OFI is the Primary Contact by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change the Primary Contact and transfer the request to another portal account, email portal support at support@templeton.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Leader / Principal Investigator information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide required information and upload the Project Leader's CV/resume; the Project Leader takes overall leadership of the project and may be the Primary Contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Project Leader is an academic, provide their 16-digit ORCiD ID number. If the Project Leader differs from the Primary Contact, include their details and CV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Co-Leader information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide required information and upload the Project Co-Leader's CV/resume if applicable; Co-Leader works alongside Project Leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Co-Leader is an academic, provide their 16-digit ORCiD ID. The Co-Leader may also be the Primary Contact or there may be no Co-Leader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relatedness to Foundation (conflict/relationship disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Project Leader or Co-Leader is related to the Foundation as described in the OFI, seek advice before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer 'Yes' only if the Project Leader/Co-Leader (or their spouse or family) presently serve as a Trustee, Officer, or staff member of the Foundation. If related as defined, email programofficer@templeton.org for further advice. Serving on the Board of Advisors in the past does not require a 'Yes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional personnel listing
rubrics_metrics.description: For each additional personnel already committed, provide full name, disciplinary and organizational affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional personnel may include co-leaders, consultants, postdocs, presenters, speakers, panelists, or other required roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: How you learned about the Foundation / prior interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how you or team members learned about the Foundation and any prior applications, funding, events, or staff discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose prior engagement with the Foundation, previous applications or awards, and conversations with staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization location and identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the country/area where the organization seeking funding is located and provide full organizational name (no abbreviations) and department/center information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide alternative names or translations if applicable. If certain organizational answers trigger restrictions, email programofficer@templeton.org as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual capacity funding indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: If seeking funding in your individual capacity (funds paid to you personally rather than an organization), indicate 'Yes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes awards payable to individuals from organizational grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure Responsibility (ER) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: If your organization is For Profit, not classified as a U.S. Public Charity, or a newly formed Public Charity with limited budget/history, the IRS requires Expenditure Responsibility (ER).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ER applies and the request is approved, you must operate under ER and provide JTF with Expenditure Responsibility Reports for grant duration, including reporting capital expenditures purchased with grant funds. Additional ER-specific details will be provided at Full Proposal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital Expenditure definition and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital expenditures generally include items with individual value ≥ $5,000 USD (or foreign equivalent) and useful life > 1 year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Equipment (vehicles, office equipment, computer equipment, research/lab equipment, aggregated equipment used together), Website (application and infrastructure development, domain acquisition, software/database/back-end/front-end), Software (development, apps, databases).

rubrics_metrics.name: What is NOT a capital expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: Items below $5,000 USD or foreign equivalent, items with useful life < 1 year, and certain other costs are not capital expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: aggregate costs of independent items (e.g., three laptops at $2,000 each), costs to lease items, website costs related to planning, content development, and operating. Also expenditures for equipment or activities not solely used for the proposed project should not be counted as Additional Funding (see Budget guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: JTF restrictions on capital expenditures and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: JTF has limits on capital expenditures relative to project duration and useful life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JTF internal ER grants have a 33-month max duration which may limit ability to fund capital expenditures with useful life >3 years. Capital expenditures with useful life exceeding 5 years (e.g., office furniture) may NOT be purchased with JTF funds. Buildings and significant building improvements may NOT be purchased with JTF grant funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted grant payment currencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation awards and pays grants in sixteen specific currencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted currencies: USD, AUD, CAD, CHF, DKK, EUR, GBP, HKD, ILS, JPY, MXN, NZD, SEK, SGD, TRY, ZAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request amount format and indirect costs/overhead limit
rubrics_metrics.description: State how much funding you are requesting; the Foundation will approve an added component for overhead/indirect costs up to 15%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round to the nearest whole currency unit and use numbers only. The Foundation welcomes proposals requesting a lower overhead percentage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Project Amount and Additional Funding expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Project Amount may be equal to or greater than the Request Amount; Foundation favors projects where a proportion of funding is secured from other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total Project Amount = Request Amount + funding secured or requested specifically for this project from other sources. For each potential source list amount and status. Additional Funding can include funds from other philanthropic organizations, in-kind support from employers of project personnel, or donated time of project members. Additional Funding does NOT include costs for equipment not solely used for the proposed project, costs for activities associated but not specifically part of the proposed project, or support for activities that occur before/after the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Narrative purpose and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a broad overview of estimated project expenses to help the Foundation determine whether amounts are reasonable and necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit narrative or bullet-point overview including anticipated amounts and major expenditure categories. Also list supplementary sources of funding, amounts, and request status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form completeness, character limits, and submission finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the OFI for completeness and character-limit conformity before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Review and Submit page allows download of the current form and identifies missing fields or fields exceeding character limits. Once submitted, the record becomes read-only and cannot be edited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answering required fields and quality of responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer questions as thoroughly and specifically as possible; required questions are marked with an asterisk (*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all mandatory fields and provide sufficient detail to allow staff to evaluate the OFI. Direct questions to programofficer@templeton.org if unclear.
